name: call-log-row
title: Call log row
description: A call in a log: caller, direction as a drawn arrow and a word, time and duration, with a voicemail, a note and a call back button.
docs: Put the rows in a ul. call is { id, name, image, number, direction, at, duration, voicemail, note }: direction is incoming, outgoing or missed, duration is in seconds, and voicemail is { duration }. A caller without a name leads with the number, written for the locale (bare numbers are grouped, +1 numbers as (415) 555-0132; a number that already has spaces or dashes is shown as written; for exact national formats pass formatted text), and says Not in contacts. A missed call is marked by its word, a heavier name and a broken arrow as well as its colour. The row reads as one sentence, Missed call from Anna de Vries, 14:32, and Call back Anna de Vries is a button of its own: onCallBack may return a promise, and the button shows a spinner while it runs; if it rejects, the row says Could not call Anna de Vries. Try again. in a short alert under the line (labels.callFailed), and each press of the button is announced, also a repeat on the same person. onOpen makes the whole row a button under the others. onNote adds a note button, showNote prints call.note under the line, onPlayVoicemail draws a play button beside the voicemail length, and playSlot replaces it with your own player. Pass now to get Yesterday in server HTML; times use locale and timeZone (en-GB gives 14:32). The row reads its own width: narrow, the time sits beside the name, the length joins the arrow and the number gives way; the note button then gives way to onOpen.
